blocks.prompt: 4 An object of mass \(m\) is thrown vertically upward. Assuming that the air resistance is proportional to its velocity at any time \(t\), construct a differential equation representing the velocity \(v\). Also, deduce the equation in the case when air resistance is negligible.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh mechanics se model banane ka sawal hai; yahan Newton's second law kaam aayega: mass \(\times\) acceleration = kul force.
Upar ki taraf ko positive maan lete hain.
Do forces hain: wazan \(mg\) neeche ki taraf, aur hawa ki mukhalifat (air resistance) \(kv\) harkat ke ulat.
Find kya karna hai? \(v\) ki equation, pehle hawa ke saath, phir hawa ke baghair.
steps:
Diya gaya: mass \(m\), cheez upar phenki gayi; air resistance velocity \(v\) ke proportional.
Maloom karna: \(v(t)\) ki differential equation, air resistance ke saath aur us ke baghair.
Tareeqa: Newton's second law \(m\frac{dv}{dt} = \) net force, upar ki taraf positive.

Forces pehchaniye
Wazan: \(-mg\) (neeche ki taraf, is liye minus).
Air resistance: \(\propto v\), is liye us ki miqdaar \(kv\) hai (\(k \ge 0\)), aur woh harkat ke ulat hai: \(-kv\).
Kyun: hawa hamesha harkat ke ulat dhakelti hai. \(-kv\) likhne ka faida yeh hai ke jab cheez upar ja rahi ho (\(v > 0\)) to force neeche hai, aur jab gir rahi ho (\(v < 0\)) to force upar; ek hi formula dono halaton mein sahi.
Yeh sign wala faisla is sawal ki jaan hai. Sochiye: gend upar ja rahi ho to hawa use neeche dabati hai, aur neeche aa rahi ho to hawa use upar rokti hai. \(-kv\) yeh dono kaam khud kar leta hai.

Newton's second law lagaiye
\[m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -mg - kv\]
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g - \dfrac{k}{m}v\]
Kyun: acceleration \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) hai; \(m\) se divide karne par \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) akela reh jata hai.
Dhyan dein: \(mg\) ko \(m\) se divide karein to sirf \(g\) bachta hai, aur \(kv\) ko \(m\) se divide karein to \(\frac{k}{m}v\).

Jab air resistance na hone ke barabar ho
\(k = 0\) rakhiye:
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g\]
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\]
Kyun: hawa na ho to sirf wazan ki force bachti hai, is liye acceleration \(-g\) hai; yahi free fall hai jo aap physics mein parh chuke hain.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(k = 0\) rakhna hi "air resistance negligible" ka matlab hai, kyunke resistance \(kv\) hai aur \(k = 0\) se woh khatam ho jati hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(v = \left(v_{0} + \frac{mg}{k}\right)e^{-kt/m} - \frac{mg}{k}\) pehli equation ko poora karta hai, aur \(k \to 0\) par yeh \(v = v_{0} - gt\) ban jata hai jo \(\frac{dv}{dt} = -g\) ko poora karta hai (dono sympy se check kiye). Answer key \(\frac{dv}{dt} = -g - \frac{k}{m}v,\ k \ge 0\) aur \(\frac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\) deti hai; jawab milta hai.
blocks.final_answer: With air resistance: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g - \dfrac{k}{m}v\) (\(k \ge 0\), \(g\) = acceleration due to gravity). Air resistance negligible: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\).
